AboutTEDx.title: About
AboutTEDx.description: In the spirit of discovering and spreading ideas, TED has created a program called TEDx. TEDx is a program of local, self-organized events that bring people together to share a TED-like experience. Our event is called TEDxDamascus where x = independently organized TED event. At our TEDxDamascus event, TED Talks video and live speakers will combine to spark deep discussion and connection in a small group. The TED Conference provides general guidance for the TEDx program, but individual TEDx events, including ours, are self-organized.

tedxDamascus.title: About TEDx Damascus
tedxDamascus.description: TEDx Damascus is an intellectual and cultural platform, organized locally and independently under an official license from TED. From one of the oldest and most inspiring capitals on Earth, we open a new window to highlight exceptional ideas, pioneering initiatives, and Syrian minds creating solutions for the future. Under our 2026 theme, "Damascus.. Where the Story is Retold", we do not merely stand on the ruins of the past; rather, we write a contemporary chapter pulsing with life and hope. Through this event, we strive to create a safe and stimulating space that brings together changemakers to exchange visions that enhance social cohesion, support innovation, and transform challenges into real opportunities. We believe that Damascus holds voices capable of profound impact and ideas that deserve to cross borders to inspire the whole world.

ted.title: About TED
ted.description: TED is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization devoted to spreading ideas, usually in the form of short, powerful talks. TED began in 1984 as a conference where Technology, Entertainment and Design converged, and today covers almost all topics — from science to business to global issues — in more than 110 languages. Meanwhile, independently run TEDx events help share ideas in communities around the world.TED's open and free initiatives for spreading ideas include TED.com, where new TED Talk videos are posted daily; TEDx, which licenses thousands of individuals and groups to host local, self-organized TED-style events around the world; the TED Fellows program, which selects innovators from around the globe to amplify the impact of their remarkable projects and activities; The Audacious Project, which surfaces and funds critical ideas that have the potential to impact millions of lives; TED Translators, which crowdsources the subtitling of TED Talks so that big ideas can spread across languages and borders; and the educational initiative TED-Ed.

AnswersPage.weeklyDescription: Every week, we explore the intersection of ancient wisdom and modern innovation. Share your perspective and join the conversation.
AnswersPage.mockAnswer1: The modular nature of Damascene wood inlay (Mosaic) is essentially early low-poly design — geometry repeated at human scale. Each piece locks into the next the way ideas lock into a community when they are shared carefully.
AnswersPage.mockAnswer2: Culture is not something we inherit — it is something we actively shape every day.
AnswersPage.mockAnswer3: Hope travels fastest when it is carried by many voices at once.
AnswersPage.mockAnswer4: Education that meets people where they are can unlock futures no wall could predict.
AnswersPage.mockAnswer5: Art in public space reminds a city that it still belongs to everyone who walks through it.
AnswersPage.mockAnswer6: Listening without rushing to fix is a radical act of respect.
AnswersPage.mockAnswer7: Small consistent actions compound into movements larger than any single headline.
AnswersPage.mockAnswer8: Technology is only as human as the empathy we bake into its first line of code.
AnswersPage.mockAnswer9: The best ideas survive not because they are loud, but because they are useful.
AnswersPage.mockAnswer10: Community safety starts with trust built in ordinary Tuesday conversations.

TeamMember.m1Bio1: Omar Al-Khatib has dedicated the last decade to transforming the narrative of the Middle East through the TEDx platform. As the lead organizer and operations director for TEDx Damascus, he bridges the gap between local innovation and global audiences.
TeamMember.m1Bio2: With a background in architectural engineering and cultural preservation, Omar views event curation as a structural challenge: how to build a stage that can support the weight of transformative ideas without collapsing into noise.
TeamMember.m1Initiative1Desc: Guiding the next generation of regional curators to maintain the TED quality standards.
TeamMember.m1Initiative2Desc: Digitizing historical Damascus oral histories for future talk inspiration.
TeamMember.m2Bio1: Lina Safadi shapes every touchpoint an attendee has with TEDx Damascus, from the first invitation email to the last handshake on event night.
TeamMember.m2Bio2: A trained hospitality strategist, she believes an idea lands harder when the room around it feels considered, so she obsesses over the small, human details most teams overlook.
TeamMember.m2Initiative1Desc: Redesigning the end-to-end experience from RSVP to post-event follow-up.
TeamMember.m2Initiative2Desc: Building a faster, warmer induction process for new team members.
TeamMember.m3Bio1: Samer Hamwi keeps the TEDx Damascus platform running, from the ticketing flow to the live-stream page thousands of people refresh on event day.
TeamMember.m3Bio2: He treats performance and accessibility as non-negotiable, and would rather rebuild a component from scratch than ship one that excludes someone.
TeamMember.m3Initiative1Desc: Cutting load times across the site ahead of the next ticket release.
TeamMember.m3Initiative2Desc: Packaging internal tools so other TEDx chapters can reuse them.
TeamMember.m4Bio1: Dina Al-Homsi turns a single stage moment into a week of stories: reels, recaps, and the quiet behind-the-scenes shots that make an audience feel like they were in the room.
TeamMember.m4Bio2: She trained as a documentary photographer before joining TEDx Damascus, and it shows in how patiently she waits for the real, unscripted moment.
TeamMember.m4Initiative1Desc: A short-form video series introducing each speaker before they take the stage.
TeamMember.m4Initiative2Desc: Restoring and captioning footage from earlier TEDx Damascus events.
TeamMember.m5Bio1: Zaid Murad is usually the first person a journalist or partner organization talks to about TEDx Damascus, and he treats every one of those conversations as the event's first impression.
TeamMember.m5Bio2: He came up through community radio, which taught him to explain big ideas simply, a skill he now points at press releases instead of broadcast scripts.
TeamMember.m5Initiative1Desc: Building relationships with regional outlets ahead of the next event cycle.
TeamMember.m5Initiative2Desc: Drafting a response playbook so the team is never caught off guard.
TeamMember.m6Bio1: Hani Jaber is the person who makes sure a stage, a badge printer, and three hundred chairs are all in the same room at the same time.
TeamMember.m6Bio2: A former logistics officer, he plans every event backward from doors-open, and keeps a running list of everything that went wrong last time so it never happens twice.
TeamMember.m6Initiative1Desc: Building a vetted list of local vendors to speed up event-day setup.
TeamMember.m6Initiative2Desc: Standardizing event-day timelines so nothing is left to memory.
TeamMember.m7Bio1: Maya Kassem spends most of the year listening, to researchers, artists, and organizers across Syria, looking for the idea that hasn't had a stage yet.
TeamMember.m7Bio2: A former university lecturer, she coaches every speaker personally through their talk, from the first rough outline to the final rehearsal.
TeamMember.m7Initiative1Desc: Expanding speaker scouting beyond Damascus to cities across Syria.
TeamMember.m7Initiative2Desc: A structured rehearsal process to help first-time speakers find their story.
TeamMember.m8Bio1: Fadi Mansour designs the systems behind the systems: the APIs, the data pipelines, and the infrastructure that let the rest of the team move fast without breaking things.
TeamMember.m8Bio2: He spent years building backend systems for fintech before TEDx Damascus, and now applies the same rigor to something with a lot less money and a lot more meaning on the line.
TeamMember.m8Initiative1Desc: Migrating legacy endpoints to a faster, more reliable API layer.
TeamMember.m8Initiative2Desc: Preparing backend infrastructure to handle traffic spikes on event day.
